bull_bear.body:
- Nearly zero debt company; Debt-to-Equity declined from 0.10 (FY23) to 0.00 (FY26).
- Issued 75,00,000 bonus equity shares (2:1 ratio) in 2025, raising authorized capital from ₹5 crore to ₹15 crore and paid-up capital to ₹11.25 crore.
- Listed on the BSE Mainboard platform in 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Leading apparel manufacturer specialising in woven bottom wear, serving 20+ globally renowned brands with premium quality, craftsmanship and innovation; 100% customer retention rate across 12 export countries.
- Four decades of industry expertise (founded 1982) with vertical integration via in-house washing and embroidery capabilities delivering 'best in industry' wash effects.
- Geographic revenue mix (FY26) skewed to Europe (58.66%) and USA (27.12%), with Asia Pacific (10.86%), Oceania (3.14%) and other markets (0.23%) rounding out exports.
- Strong relationships with marquee global clients, reinforced by participation in major international trade fairs (Texworld Paris, Magic Las Vegas, Premiere Vision Paris, Bharat Tex Delhi).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Diversification] Non-textile diversification into agriculture (280 acres of farmland acquired in Sirumalai, Dindigul, in 1993 for cultivation of coffee, pepper and seasonal fruits) and solar energy.
- [Industry tailwind] India is the world's 2nd-largest textile producer and 6th-largest T&A exporter; Indian T&A industry projected to grow 15-20% CAGR to 2030 with exports reaching US$350bn, backed by PM MITRA/ELI/RoSCTL schemes, a ₹5,272 Cr Union Budget allocation for the Ministry of Textiles, and 100% automatic-route FDI.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Meenakshi India as a four-decade-old, vertically integrated woven bottom-wear manufacturer serving marquee global apparel brands, pursuing capacity expansion, product/geography diversification and near-zero-debt balance sheet strength.
